title: Black Obelisk tribute claim of “Iaua bit Khumri” (Jehu)
summary: Shalmaneser III’s annals for 841 BC list tribute from “Iaua of the house of Omri”, usually read as Jehu.
description: Shalmaneser III’s annals for 841 BC list tribute from “Iaua of the house of Omri”, usually read as Jehu. Event record added from Griffith & White’s Reply to Beckman, Part 2 (Table 1, row 841 (Black Obelisk, Iaua bit Khumry tribute), p. 37; section “The Black Obelisk - Jehu”, pp. 10–11).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 2): 841 BC (annal year of the claim).

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 2: An Objectivist Answer to the Assyrian Synchronisms," OSF preprint v2.10 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DT6GX, Table 1, row 841 (Black Obelisk, Iaua bit Khumry tribute), p. 37; section “The Black Obelisk - Jehu”, pp. 10–11
chronologies.note: CFAH: an anachronistic reference to Jehu. The authors think the tribute was most probably paid during Ashur-nasirpal’s undated Amuq Valley campaign, shortly before year 18 (865 BC), or possibly early in Shalmaneser III’s reign; or that “Iaua bit Khumri” was Jehoram of Israel.
